workarounds.symptom: data: DataStore.open leaks the connection when post-connect setup fails
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(data): create gflow.db readable only by its owner. Target files: src/gflow_cli/data/store.py, src/gflow_cli/winsec.py, .github/workflows/ci.yml. `gflow.db` was created with default permissions, so on a typical Linux system other local users could read the prompts and queued jobs in it. This change creates the database readable only by its owner and tightens an existing one when gflow opens it for writing. (Ref: https://github.com/ffroliva/gflow-cli/pull/1493)

workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(mcp): set isError from one failure set shared with telemetry (#1464). The set lives in a small module, `mcp/envelope_status.py` (`FAILURE_STATUSES`, `is_failure`), which both `GflowMCPServer.call_tool` and `tools.outcome_of` use, so a status that telemetry counts as a failure can no longer reach the client with `isError: false`. It's a s... (Ref: https://github.com/ffroliva/gflow-cli/pull/1479)

workarounds.symptom: test: showlocals redaction test matches its token fragment inside a memory address
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(test): strip hex addresses before checking showlocals redaction (#1429). Target files: tests/test_e2e_env_redaction.py. `tests/test_e2e_env_redaction.py::test_truncated_gh_token_under_showlocals_shows_no_fragment` failed in CI (run 45008256814) with no secret leaking: `--showlocals` prints object reprs with hex memory addresses, and the token fragment `abcd` happened to occur inside one (`<_pytest.monkeypatch.MonkeyPatch object at 0x7a873abcdb80>`). A re-run passed. (Ref: https://github.com/ffroliva/gflow-cli/pull/1440)

workarounds.symptom: image batch on flow.google.com: traceback and exit 1 instead of exit 36
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(image): report image batch failures instead of crashing (#1452). Target files: src/gflow_cli/cli_image.py, tests/cli/test_cli_image.py, CHANGELOG.md. `image batch` called `asyncio.run(run_manifest_image_batch(...))` with no error handling, so a `GFlowError` raised before any prompt ran reached Click as a traceback with exit 1. On flow.google.com that is `FlowHostMigratedError` on every run, although `docs/USAGE.md` and `docs/CAPABILITIES.md` say `image batch` exits 36 there. It now goes through `_handle_gflow_error`, ... (Ref: https://github.com/ffroliva/gflow-cli/pull/1454)

workarounds.symptom: flow.google.com: a new-project click that times out crashes with exit 1
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(migrated): a new-project click that times out is exit 23, not a crash. Target files: scripts/dev/spike_create_click_timeout.py, src/gflow_cli/api/transports/_mc_common.py, src/gflow_cli/api/transports/migrated_composer.py. - `create_project` on `flow.google.com` passed the bare Create click to `rpc_reply`, which wraps only its own reply timeout. A Playwright click timeout (not a subclass of the builtin `TimeoutError`) escaped as an unhandled exit 1. This is the largest crash group in the first week of usage telemetry ... (Ref: https://github.com/ffroliva/gflow-cli/pull/1435)

workarounds.symptom: exit 23 "0 option groups rendered" with GFLOW_CLI_BROWSER_ENGINE=patchright is the pinned patchright 1.61.2 .last.count() bug, not Flow UI drift
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(deps): bump patchright extra to 1.64.4 so .last locators resolve (#1319). Target files: pyproject.toml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, tests/api/test_engine_locator_contract.py. With `GFLOW_CLI_BROWSER_ENGINE=patchright`, every generation on flow.google.com failed with exit 23 "0 option groups rendered" before submit. Flow's UI had not changed. The cause is the pinned `patchright==1.61.2`: in that release, `locator.last` and `locator.nth(-1)` count `0` whenever exactly one element matches. The migrated composer resolves it... (Ref: https://github.com/ffroliva/gflow-cli/pull/1321)

Fixes UiSelectorDriftError (exit 23) in the migrated host settings pane when driving non-English accounts (e.g. German hl=de). (Ref: https://github.com/ffroliva/gflow-cli/pull/1315)
